label: Fires at D2 after choosing a2, most when switching to a2 or against S1-favoring belief.
short_terms: (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * last_is('a1 S1 u') ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * belief ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2)
terms: (phase == D2) * (action == 2) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (stay == 0) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == 2) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * np.abs(belief_lo) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (belief_lo > 0) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_reward == 0)
explanation: Silent at D1 and GO; only fires at D2 and only after an a2 choice (seen as in_action at D2, so observed). Magnitude is largest when the a2 choice is a switch from a1 (weight ~0.76), larger when the observer belief still favors S1 (a2 chosen against or with weak evidence, ~0.3), and slightly larger after an unrewarded previous trial. Reached state, hidden good state and trials since reversal add little. The free fit adds the trial-before reward, reached state S2, and a negative correction for staying on a2 after a loss; it gains only ~0.06 over the short form. Remaining variance is large-magnitude stays on a2 after losses that the indicator terms only partly capture.

issues: The label and explanation say the main driver is any switch to a2. It is really one kind of switch: a2 after a common-unrewarded a1 trial (a1 S1 u, the model-based switch). Adding (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * last_is('a1 S1 u') to the stay and belief terms gives it weight +0.83 and drops the generic stay==0 weight from 0.76 to 0.32. Test R^2 beyond timing rises from 0.42 to 0.49.

Misses on the recorded short form show a systematic error by previous trial. D2 after a1 S2 r (a rare-rewarded a1 trial, then a switch to a2) is over-predicted by -0.228. D2 after a2 S1 r is under-predicted by +0.115 and D2 after a1 S1 u by +0.068. So the stay==0 term lumps two different switch types together.
The prev_reward==0 term adds almost nothing. Its weight is +0.067, and test R^2 is 0.420 without it vs 0.431 with it. It works as a filler correction, not a real driver.

The belief claim holds in direction: given a2, activation is higher when P(S1 good) is higher. A continuous belief term (0.440) beats belief_lo>0 (0.421) and np.abs(belief_lo) (0.367). The 'weak evidence' reading is not supported separately: an np.abs(belief_lo)<1 term gets weight 0.04.
The better short form scores 0.494 test R^2 beyond timing, slightly above the reported free fit (0.491). With it, the remaining misses are small and balanced (largest is +0.059 at D2 after a2 S1 r).
